strategies.name: Baseline Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with intermediate element-wise scaling and division operations, matching the reference implementation structure. Dispatch count is 8 all-reduces plus local ops (clones, scaling). Represents the simplest approach with no fusion or overlap, trading implementation simplicity for higher latency due to sequential dependencies.

strategies.name: Fused Local Operations Between All-Reduces
strategies.desc: Keeps 8 all-reduce operations but fuses all local element-wise operations (scaling by a[r]/W, division by a[r]) into single kernel launches between collectives, eliminating intermediate clone() calls where possible. Dispatch count remains 8 all-reduces but reduces local-op dispatches from ~24 to ~8. Trades code complexity for reduced memory traffic and fewer kernel launches.

strategies.name: Pre-computed Weight Matrices
strategies.desc: Pre-computes all scaling factors as diagonal weight matrices or broadcasted tensors before the loop, then uses fused multiply-add operations between all-reduces. Dispatch count is 8 all-reduces with streamlined local ops. Reduces redundant computation of a[r] values in each iteration, trading small upfront memory allocation for faster per-iteration local computation.

strategies.name: Pipelined All-Reduce with Split Buffers
strategies.desc: Splits the global buffer into chunks and pipelines all-reduce operations across different chunks to overlap communication with local computation. Uses multiple buffers to allow next iteration's local ops while current all-reduce is in-flight. Dispatch count is still 8 all-reduces but with overlapped execution. Trades increased memory footprint (2-3x buffers) for reduced wall-clock time through pipeline parallelism.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction Pattern
strategies.desc:
Exploits the structure of 224=32×7 or similar factorizations to perform intra-node and inter-node reductions separately in a hierarchical pattern, potentially reducing the number of global all-reduces by batching operations within node boundaries. Dispatch count could be reduced to ~4-6 global all-reduces plus node-local reductions. Trades algorithmic complexity and careful rank-topology mapping for lower cross-node bandwidth consumption.
